cases.sentence: ___, носивший письмо, передал ей самый жестокий и неожиданный ею ответ, что ответа не будет.
cases.translation: The messenger who carried the letter delivered to her the cruelest and most unexpected answer: that there would be no answer.
cases.explain: «Комиссионер» is the subject of «передал» (delivered), so it stands in the Nominative case.

cases.sentence: ...разрешение видеть сына должно зависеть от великодушия ___.
cases.translation: ...permission to see her son must depend on her husband's magnanimity.
cases.explain: The preposition «от» (from/on) governs the Genitive case: «от великодушия мужа».

cases.sentence: ...так ей возмутительно показалась эта злоба в сравнении с ее страстную законную нежностью к ___...
cases.translation: ...this malice seemed so outrageous to her next to her passionate, legitimate tenderness for her son...
cases.explain: The preposition «к» governs the Dative case: «к сыну».

cases.sentence: Она поехала в игрушечную ___, накупила игрушек и обдумала план действий.
cases.translation: She went to the toy shop, bought a quantity of toys, and worked out her plan of action.
cases.explain: The preposition «в» expressing motion into a place governs the Accusative case: «в лавку».

cases.sentence: Она не могла и не хотела поделиться им с ___.
cases.translation: She could not and would not share it with Vronsky.
cases.explain: The preposition «с» (with) governs the Instrumental case: «с Вронским».

cases.sentence: ...но няня уже не находилась в ___ Алексея Александровича.
cases.translation: ...but the nurse no longer lived in Alexei Alexandrovich's house.
cases.explain: The preposition «в» (in) governs the Prepositional case: «в доме».

reading.ru: Одна из целей поездки в Россию для Анны было свидание с сыном.
reading.question: What was one of Anna's goals in traveling to Russia?
reading.correct: To see her son
reading.explain: The text says one of the purposes of Anna's trip to Russia was to see her son.

reading.ru: Но по приезде в Петербург ей вдруг представилось ясное ее теперешнее положение в обществе, и она поняла, что устроить свидание было трудно.
reading.question: What did Anna realize upon arriving in Petersburg?
options: That arranging the meeting with her son would be difficult given her position in society
That she no longer wanted to see her son
reading.correct: That arranging the meeting with her son would be difficult given her position in society
reading.explain: On arriving in Petersburg, her present position in society suddenly became clear to her, and she understood the meeting would be difficult to arrange.

reading.ru: Поехать прямо в дом, где можно было встретиться с Алексеем Александровичем, она чувствовала, что не имела права.
reading.question: Why didn't Anna go directly to her former home?
options: She felt she had no right to, risking being turned away and insulted
She did not know the address
reading.correct: She felt she had no right to, risking being turned away and insulted
reading.explain: The text says she felt she had no right to go straight to the house where she might meet Alexei Alexandrovich.

reading.ru: Старая няня Сережа могла помочь ей и научить ее, но няня уже не находилась в доме Алексея Александровича.
reading.question: Why couldn't Seryozha's old nurse help Anna?
options: The nurse no longer worked in Alexei Alexandrovich's household
The nurse refused to help her
reading.correct: The nurse no longer worked in Alexei Alexandrovich's household
reading.explain: The text says the old nurse could have helped her, but she no longer lived in Alexei Alexandrovich's house.

reading.ru: Анна на третий день решилась написать ей стоившее ей большого труда письмо, в котором она умышленно говорила, что разрешение видеть сына должно зависеть от великодушия мужа.
reading.question: What did Anna do on the third day?
options: She wrote a difficult letter to Lidia Ivanovna, framing permission to see her son as dependent on her husband's generosity
reading.correct: She wrote a difficult letter to Lidia Ivanovna, framing permission to see her son as dependent on her husband's generosity
reading.explain: On the third day Anna decided to write a letter, costing her great effort, saying permission to see her son should depend on her husband's magnanimity.

reading.ru: Комиссионер, носивший письмо, передал ей самый жестокий и неожиданный ею ответ, что ответа не будет.
reading.question: What answer did the messenger bring back to Anna?
options: That there would be no answer at all
A written refusal explaining the reasons
reading.correct: That there would be no answer at all
reading.explain: The messenger who carried the letter brought her the cruelest, most unexpected answer: that there would be no answer.

reading.ru: Она никогда не чувствовала себя столь униженную, как в ту минуту, когда, призвав комиссионера, услышала от него подробный рассказ о том, как он дожидался, и как потом ему сказали «ответа никакого не будет».
reading.question: How did Anna feel upon hearing the messenger's report?
options: She had never felt so humiliated
reading.correct: She had never felt so humiliated
reading.explain: The text says she never felt so humiliated as in that moment, hearing the messenger's account.

reading.ru: Она не могла и не хотела поделиться им с Вронским.
reading.question: Why didn't Anna share her grief with Vronsky?
options: She believed he would never understand the depth of her suffering and feared his cold reaction
She had promised not to mention her son
reading.correct: She believed he would never understand the depth of her suffering and feared his cold reaction
reading.explain: The text says she could not and would not share her grief with Vronsky, knowing he would never grasp the depth of her suffering.

reading.ru: Просидев дома целый день, она придумывала средства для свидания с сыном и остановилась на решении написать мужу.
reading.question: After a day of thinking, what did Anna decide to do?
options: Give up on seeing her son
reading.correct: Write to her husband
reading.explain: Having sat at home the whole day devising means to see her son, she settled on the decision to write to her husband.

reading.ru: Молчание графини смирило и покорило ее, но письмо, все то, что она прочла между его строками, так раздражило ее, так ей возмутительно показалась эта злоба в сравнении с ее страстную законную нежностью к сыну, что она возмутилась против других и перестала обвинять себя».
reading.question: What effect did Lidia Ivanovna's letter have on Anna?
options: It infuriated her, even though the countess's earlier silence had subdued her
It made her forgive her husband
It convinced her to stay away from her son
reading.correct: It infuriated her, even though the countess's earlier silence had subdued her
reading.explain: The text says the countess's silence had subdued her, but the letter and what she read between its lines so irritated her that she stopped blaming herself.

reading.ru: И тут же она решила, что завтра же, в самый день рождения Сережи, она поедет прямо в дом мужа, подкупит людей, будет обманывать, но во что бы то ни стало увидит сына и разрушит этот безобразный обман, которым они окружили несчастного ребенка.
reading.question: What did Anna resolve to do on Seryozha's birthday?
options: To go straight to her husband's house and see her son no matter what
To send a birthday gift by mail
To ask Vronsky to go instead
reading.correct: To go straight to her husband's house and see her son no matter what
reading.explain: She resolved that on Seryozha's birthday she would go straight to her husband's house, bribe the servants, and see her son whatever it took.

reading.ru: Она поехала в игрушечную лавку, накупила игрушек и обдумала план действий.
reading.question: What did Anna do to prepare for the visit?
options: She went to a toy shop and bought toys, then planned her approach
She hired a lawyer to gain custody
She wrote a long letter to Seryozha
She asked Betsy to accompany her
reading.correct: She went to a toy shop and bought toys, then planned her approach
reading.explain: The text says she went to a toy shop, bought toys, and thought over her plan of action.

reading.ru: На другой день в восемь часов утра Анна вышла одна из извозчичей кареты и позвонила у большого подъезда своего бывшего дома.
reading.question: What did Anna do the next morning at eight o'clock?
options: She got out of a cab alone and rang the bell at her former home's entrance
She sent a servant ahead of her
She met Seryozha in the park
reading.correct: She got out of a cab alone and rang the bell at her former home's entrance
reading.explain: The next day at eight in the morning, Anna got out of a hired carriage alone and rang at the main entrance of her former home.

reading.ru: Помощник швейцара, незнакомый Анне Молодой-Малой, только что отворил ей дверь, как она уже вошла в нее и, вынув из муфты трехрублевую бумажку, поспешно сунула ему в руку.
reading.question: How did Anna get past the unfamiliar assistant doorman?
options: She slipped in as soon as he opened the door and gave him money
She showed a letter of permission
She pretended to be a relative of the family
reading.correct: She slipped in as soon as he opened the door and gave him money
reading.explain: As soon as the assistant doorman opened the door, she stepped in and quickly pressed a three-ruble note into his hand.

reading.ru: Заметив замешательство неизвестной, сам Капитоныч вышел к ней, пропустил в двери и спросил, что ей угодно.
reading.question: Who came out to help the mysterious veiled visitor?
reading.correct: Kapitonych himself
reading.explain: Noticing the unknown lady's confusion, Kapitonych himself came out to her, let her through the door, and asked what she wanted.

reading.ru: Сняв шубку, Капитоныч заглянул ей в лицо, узнал ее и молча низко поклонился ей.
reading.question: What happened when Kapitonych removed her fur coat?
options: He recognized her face and silently bowed low to her
He asked her to leave immediately
reading.correct: He recognized her face and silently bowed low to her
reading.explain: As he took off her fur coat, Kapitonych glanced at her face, recognized her, and bowed low without a word.

reading.ru: По одному голосу этого зеванья она узнала сына и как живого увидала его пред собою.
reading.question: How did Anna recognize her son before even seeing him?
options: By the sound of his yawn
By his voice calling her name
reading.correct: By the sound of his yawn
reading.explain: By the sound of the yawn alone, she recognized her son and saw him vividly as if before her.

reading.ru: «Сережа!» — прошептала она, неслышно подходя к нему.
reading.question: What did Anna do upon seeing her son in bed?
options: She whispered his name as she approached silently
reading.correct: She whispered his name as she approached silently
reading.explain: The text says she whispered 'Seryozha!' as she approached him inaudibly.

reading.ru: «Мама!» — проговорил он, двигаясь под ее руками, чтобы разными местами тела касаться ее рук.
reading.question: How did Seryozha react upon recognizing his mother?
options: He said "Mama!" and pressed close to her, wanting to touch her with his whole body
He cried and pushed her away
He asked where she had been for so long
He immediately fell back asleep without speaking
reading.correct: He said "Mama!" and pressed close to her, wanting to touch her with his whole body
reading.explain: He said 'Mama!' moving under her hands so as to touch her with different parts of his body.

reading.ru: «Я знал», — открывая глаза, сказал он, — «нынче мое рождение.
reading.question: What did Seryozha say he had known would happen on his birthday?
options: That he would receive a new toy
That his father would be there
reading.correct: That his mother would come
reading.explain: Opening his eyes, he says he knew it was his birthday and that his mother would come.

reading.ru: «О чем же ты плачешь, мама?» — сказал он, совершенно проснувшись.
reading.question: What did Seryozha ask when he saw his mother crying?
reading.correct: Why she was crying
reading.explain: Now fully awake, he asks, 'Why are you crying, Mama?'
